'''Timm Lane Rosenbach''' (born October 27, 1966) is an American [[college football]] coach and former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player. He was most recently the co-[[offensive coordinator]] and [[wide receiver]]s coach for [[California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo]], a position he held from 2024 through 2025. Rosenbach was the head football coach at [[Adams State Grizzlies football|Adams State University]] in [[Alamosa, Colorado]], taking the position at the [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] school in December 2014 and remaining there until he resigned in December 2017 to become the offensive coordinator at Montana.<ref>{{cite web | title=Timm Rosenbach Takes Over As Head Coach For Adams State Football | website=Adams State University Athletics | date=2014-12-22 | url=https://asugrizzlies.com/news/2014/12/22/FB_1222145626.aspx | access-date=2025-08-23}}</ref>  He played from 1989 until 1995 in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). Rosenbach attended [[Washington State University]] and was selected in the first round of the 1989 NFL supplemental draft.

Rosenbach became a coach after his retirement from the NFL, and he was hired in 1999 by NAIA school [[St. Ambrose University]] to be its quarterbacks coach. He has since gone on to work at other schools, including spending four years at his alma mater as its quarterbacks coach.

'''Timothy Gene Vogler''' (born December 20, 1956, in [[Troy, Ohio]]) is a retired [[American football]] [[Guard (American football)|guard]] who played in the [[National Football League]] for the [[Buffalo Bills]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Ohio State University]].<ref>Strode, George. [https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=266&dat=19770822&id=2d0wAAAAIBAJ&sjid=_dwFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2732,5276453 "Hayes Changing Football Philosophy"]. ''[[Kentucky New Era]]'', August 23, 1977, p. 16. Retrieved on July 23, 2013.</ref>

Vogler was not selected in the [[1979 NFL draft]], but signed with the Bills later that year.<ref name="ESPN 06">[[Pete Palmer|Palmer, Pete]]; Pullis, Ken; [[Sean Lahman|Lahman, Sean]]; Silverman, Matthew; [[Gary Gillette|Gillette, Gary]]. ''The ESPN Pro Football Encyclopedia: First Edition'', p. 697. [[ESPN Books]], 2006. {{ISBN|978-1-4027-4216-3}}.</ref> Initially a reserve, he became a full-time starter with the Bills by 1985, when he started 14 games.<ref name="ESPN 06" /> Although he also filled in at center on occasion,<ref>[[John Clayton (sportswriter)|Clayton, John]]. [https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1144&dat=19851209&id=NmodAAAAIBAJ&sjid=k2IEAAAAIBAJ&pg=6884,123844 "Bills' comedy of errors delights Jets"]. ''[[Pittsburgh Press]]'', December 9, 1985, p. D3. Retrieved on July 23, 2013.</ref> Vogler spent much of the next four seasons as Buffalo's starter at right guard.<ref name="ESPN 06" /><ref>''[[Palm Beach Post]]''. [https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1964&dat=19871026&id=1UkjAAAAIBAJ&sjid=mM4FAAAAIBAJ&pg=4061,3311419 "Offerdahl a spectator - Tackling milestones set"]. October 26, 1987, p. 12C. Retrieved on July 23, 2013.</ref> Vogler suffered a knee injury that forced him to miss the Bills' run to the [[1988-89 NFL playoffs|1989 AFC Championship]].<ref>Wilner, Barry. [https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1298&dat=19890107&id=vPhNAAAAIBAJ&sjid=a4sDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5833,696010 "Bengals to rely on ground attack"]. ''[[The Free Lance-Star]]'' (Fredericksburg, Va.), January 7, 1989, p. 12. Retrieved on July 23, 2013.</ref> After knee surgery during the off-season,<ref>''[[Schenectady Gazette]]''. [https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1917&dat=19890818&id=onYhAAAAIBAJ&sjid=VIkFAAAAIBAJ&pg=1023,4911795 "Bears trade McMahon to San Diego"]. August 19, 1989, p. 26. Retrieved on July 23, 2013.</ref> Vogler's Buffalo career ended after the 1989 preseason when he was placed on the physically unable to perform list.<ref>''[[Sun Journal (Lewiston)|Sun Journal]]'' (Lewiston, Maine). [https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1914&dat=19890830&id=TfUpAAAAIBAJ&sjid=L2UFAAAAIBAJ&pg=4539,5838465 "Transactions"]. August 30, 1989, p. 36. Retrieved on July 23, 2013.</ref>

'''Timothy Richard Tebow''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|iː|b|oʊ}}; born August 14, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for three seasons, primarily with the [[Denver Broncos]]. Tebow played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], becoming the first underclassman to win the [[Heisman Trophy]] and leading the team to two [[BCS National Championship]] titles in [[2007 BCS National Championship Game|2006]] and [[2009 BCS National Championship Game|2008]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 9, 2007 |title=Florida QB Tebow is first underclassman to win Heisman |publisher=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/news/story?id=3146714 |url-status=live |access-date=November 9, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020235051/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncf/news/story?id=3146714 |archive-date=October 20, 2012}}</ref> At the conclusion of his collegiate career, Tebow held the [[Southeastern Conference]]'s records for career [[passing efficiency]] and rushing touchdowns.<ref name="NCAA Record Book">{{Cite web |year=2011 |title=NCAA Football Bowl Subdivision Records |url=http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2011/FBS.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120915081634/http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2011/FBS.pdf |archive-date=September 15, 2012 |access-date=November 9, 2012 |publisher=[[NCAA]]}} pp. 26, 29.</ref> He was selected by the Broncos in the first round of the [[2010 NFL draft]].

Tebow became the Broncos' starter during the 2011 season and revitalized a struggling team, bringing them to the franchise's first division title and playoff victory since 2005.<ref name="Playoff exit">{{Cite magazine |date=January 14, 2012 |title=Patriots rout Broncos 45–10 in AFC playoffs |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/nfl/gameflash/2012/01/14/4834/index.html |url-status=dead |magazine=Sports Illustrated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130129115253/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/nfl/gameflash/2012/01/14/4834/index.html |archive-date=January 29, 2013 |access-date=November 9, 2012 |agency=The Associated Press}}</ref> His frequent comeback victories and outspoken Christian faith made him a cultural phenomenon, with his habit of dropping to one knee in prayer on the field becoming known as "Tebowing". Due to questions over Tebow's potential as an NFL quarterback, he was traded after the season to the [[New York Jets]], where he spent one year as a backup.<ref name="Jets release">{{Cite news |last=Garafolo |first=Mike |date=April 29, 2013 |title=Jets waive Tim Tebow after one season |work=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Gannett Company]] |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2013/04/29/tim-tebow-released-new-york-jets/2120333/ |access-date=October 8, 2021}}</ref>

After failing to make the regular season roster of the [[New England Patriots]] and [[Philadelphia Eagles]], Tebow pursued a [[Minor League Baseball|minor league]] [[baseball]] career with the [[New York Mets]] organization from 2016 to 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Martin |first=Jill |date=February 18, 2021 |title=Tim Tebow retires from baseball |publisher=[[CNN]] |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/02/18/us/tim-tebow-baseball-retirement-trnd/index.html |access-date=February 18, 2021}}</ref> The same year he retired from baseball, he returned to the NFL as a [[tight end]] for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], but was released after one preseason game. Since 2017, he has been a regular contributor and co-host for college football programming on [[SEC Network]] and [[ESPN]]. Tebow was inducted in the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2023.
